helper:splittingCoordinates.title: Inverse splitting coordinates
helper:splittingCoordinates.statement: For $r\ne0$ in a field of characteristic zero, the substitution $x_1^\prime=x_1+rx_2$, $x_2^\prime=x_1-rx_2$ has the inverse $x_1=(x_1^\prime+x_2^\prime)/2$, $x_2=(x_1^\prime-x_2^\prime)/(2r)$. The linked lemma checks the composition in this direction.
helper:splittingCoordinates.proof: Substitute the two inverse expressions into the original coordinates.

helper:polynomialFibres.title: Fibres of the polynomial map
helper:polynomialFibres.statement: Let $f=t^3-t^2+at+b\in\QQ[t]$ be separable, and suppose that $f$ either has Galois group $C_3$ or splits over $\QQ$. Exactly two rational torus points have characteristic polynomial $f$.
helper:polynomialFibres.proof: Use the two roots of the quadratic resolvent and their distinctness in the separable case.

helper:moduliFibres.title: Fibres of the moduli map
helper:moduliFibres.statement: Two $C_3$-algebras with trace-one normal elements that give the same rational quotient point are isomorphic as pairs.
helper:moduliFibres.proof: Identify both pairs with the fibre algebra over their common quotient point.

helper:supportFunctionSymmetry.title: Galois symmetry of the support function
helper:supportFunctionSymmetry.statement: For the Galois-invariant parameter $(s_0,\sigma,\sigma)$, interchanging the two conjugate coordinates leaves the support function unchanged.
helper:supportFunctionSymmetry.proof: Compare its values on the cones interchanged by the coordinate swap.

helper:weightCharacters.title: Characters of the four weight vectors
helper:weightCharacters.statement: Each of the four sections displayed in Lemma~\ref{lemma:heightformula} is a weight vector for its listed character.
helper:weightCharacters.proof: Identify the section with the corresponding eigen-monomial divided by $e_1^3$.

helper:characterCoordinates.title: Character evaluations in idempotent coordinates
helper:characterCoordinates.statement: Over a field of characteristic zero containing a primitive cube root $\zeta$, write $g=u e_0+v e_1+w e_2$ in the idempotent basis of the group algebra. The three character evaluations are $u,v,w$: \[g_0+g_1+g_2=u,\qquad g_0+\zeta g_1+\zeta^2g_2=v,\qquad g_0+\zeta^2g_1+\zeta g_2=w.\]
helper:characterCoordinates.proof: Evaluate the three characters on the three idempotents.

helper:cubicCharacters.title: The difference of the cubic characters
helper:cubicCharacters.statement: In a commutative ring, if $\zeta^2+\zeta+1=0$, then \[(x+y\zeta+z\zeta^2)^3-(x+y\zeta^2+z\zeta)^3=3(2\zeta+1)(x-z)(y-x)(z-y).\]
helper:cubicCharacters.proof: Expand the cubes and use the relation satisfied by $\zeta$.

helper:localWeightHeight.title: Local height from the weights
helper:localWeightHeight.statement: At a finite place, the local height for $3D_0$ is the square root of the maximum of $1$ and the absolute values of the three nontrivial weight characters.
helper:localWeightHeight.proof: The support function is the minimum of the four weight pairings. Exponentiating turns this minimum into the stated maximum.

helper:integralLocalHeight.title: Finite height factors at integral points
helper:integralLocalHeight.statement: At each finite prime, the local height factor for $3D_0$ is one on the integral locus.
helper:integralLocalHeight.proof: Apply the local integral conditions to the four weight values.

helper:integralCoefficients.title: Integral coefficients in Eisenstein coordinates
helper:integralCoefficients.statement:
If a rational torus point has parameter $
u=u+v\zeta$, its characteristic polynomial has integral coefficients exactly when \[N(
u)\in1+3\ZZ,\qquad N(
u)(3-\operatorname{Tr}(
u))\in1+27\ZZ.\]
helper:integralCoefficients.proof: Substitute the norm and trace in the formulas for the two cubic coefficients.

helper:adelicLogarithm.title: The finite adelic logarithm
helper:adelicLogarithm.statement: If an adele has component in the maximal compact subgroup at every prime outside a finite set $S$, its finite logarithm is the sum of the local logarithms over $S$.
helper:adelicLogarithm.proof: The logarithm vanishes on each maximal compact subgroup, so all other terms vanish.

helper:finiteIntegralProduct.title: Evaluation of the finite Fourier product
helper:finiteIntegralProduct.statement: For $\operatorname{Re}(\sigma)>1$ and $t\in\RR$, the product of the actual local Haar integrals equals the finite Euler product in Lemma~\ref{lemma:finiteFourierProduct}, with parameter $\lambda=\sigma-\pi it$.
helper:finiteIntegralProduct.proof: Identify the local integrands with the evaluated Fourier factors and multiply the convergent factors.

helper:archimedeanIntegral.title: Evaluation of the archimedean integral
helper:archimedeanIntegral.statement: For $\operatorname{Re}(s_0)>0$ and $\operatorname{Re}(\sigma)>0$, the Fourier integral in the logarithm coordinate, with Lebesgue measure, is \[\frac{s_0+2\sigma}{(s_0+2\pi it)(2\sigma-2\pi it)}.\]
helper:archimedeanIntegral.proof: Integrate separately on the two half-lines and combine the resulting fractions.

helper:correctionProduct.title: Convergence of the split correction factors
helper:correctionProduct.proof: Bound each deviation by a constant times $p^{-2\operatorname{Re}(z)}$ and compare with a convergent Dirichlet series.

helper:correctionBound.title: A bound for the Euler correction
helper:correctionBound.statement: For every $\beta>1/2$ there is a constant $C_\beta$ such that \[|(1-3^{-z})^2R(z)|\leq C_\beta\qquad(\operatorname{Re}(z)\geq\beta).\]
helper:correctionBound.proof: Bound the correction products uniformly on the half-plane and bound the factor at $3$.

helper:boundaryChain.title: Self-intersections of the boundary components
helper:boundaryChain.statement: The five components of the reduced boundary, in chain order, have self-intersections $-2,-2,-1,-2,-2$.
helper:boundaryChain.proof: Compute the adjacent primitive rays in the resolved fan.

helper:boundaryIntersection.title: The square of the reduced boundary
helper:boundaryIntersection.proof: Add the self-intersections and twice the intersections of adjacent components.

helper:leadingConstants.title: Identities for the main-term constants
helper:leadingConstants.statement: The Euler products and prime sums defining the main-term constants converge and agree with their simplified expressions.
helper:leadingConstants.proof: Combine the product identities, logarithmic derivatives, and the evaluation of the Euler--Kronecker constant.

helper:laurentRescaling.title: Rescaling the Laurent expansion
helper:laurentRescaling.statement: Substituting $s=2z$ in the Laurent expansion at $s=2$ changes its polar part to \[\frac{c_2}{4(z-1)^2}+\frac{c_1}{2(z-1)}.\]
helper:laurentRescaling.proof: Use $2z-2=2(z-1)$ in the Laurent expansion; the remainder stays bounded near $z=1$.
